record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how minibatch size and added gradient noise affect held-out accuracy, using a different intervention from the batch-size training recipes in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy curves and tables for three network configurations as minibatch size and noise-enhancement strength vary. The text describes the curves qualitatively; precise values are available for selected settings in Tables 2 and 3. Optimizer comparisons and fixed-epoch-budget comparisons are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study develops noise enhancement using the batch-size/generalization premise and evaluates its performance. All runs stop at training-loss thresholds, with learning-rate halving triggered by loss; epochs are not held fixed. Its batch-size sweeps and remedy comparisons therefore do not establish V5's budget-conditioned effect. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that suitably chosen noise enhancement improves generalization and yields higher selected mean accuracy for large batches than unenhanced smaller batches. Their explanation involving noise structure and non-Gaussianity remains intuitive rather than theoretically established. These conclusions concern Adam trained to loss thresholds, not equal epoch budgets.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a two-minibatch noise-enhancement update, varying minibatch size and α; it does not reproduce the fixed-epoch large-batch recipes in V5. Runs end at specified training-loss thresholds.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with minibatch size and noise-enhancement strength α. The authors report an optimal minibatch size for each fixed α, and say generalization improves for α not too large.

fits_no_version.finding: Without noise enhancement, accuracy depends on batch size and has an optimum; the authors describe worse generalization at larger batches even when training continues to a loss threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects held-out accuracy under loss-threshold stopping with Adam, independently of a fixed-epoch comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Suitably chosen noise enhancement improves accuracy and reduces the small-batch/large-batch gap. At B=5000, selected mean accuracies exceed the best unenhanced batch-size settings by 0.18, 0.21, and 0.13 percentage points for F1, C1, and C2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise enhancement can improve large-batch Adam generalization when training ends at specified loss thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: At separately selected optimal batch sizes, noise enhancement reduces iteration counts to the stopping threshold; at a fixed batch size, the text says it increases iteration counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise enhancement's convergence cost depends on whether batch size is held fixed or reselected.

record.problems: The experiments cover three configurations and three datasets, with 10 random initializations per setting. The reported comparisons use training-loss convergence thresholds, not a fixed epoch budget. Several curve results are available only as figures, without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported test-accuracy findings were omitted. Convergence-time rows R9–R16 are included but do not directly measure the test-error gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance on matched image tasks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences; all experiments use Adam.
The large-batch penalty with epochs held fixed, and whether an adapted recipe removes that penalty under the specified budget conditions. Training instead ends at loss thresholds.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The missing fixed-epoch comparison is an untested condition, not evidence limiting or challenging V5. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations over ten initializations. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons.
The study does not hold the number of epochs fixed; it trains to stated training-loss thresholds. It does not test language models, warmup, or normalization and regularization changes as remedies.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: C1 on CIFAR-10, F1 on Fashion-MNIST, and C2 on CIFAR-100 at the reported optimal minibatch sizes
reader_labels.reason: At the reported optima, adding noise enhancement raises test accuracy relative to α = 1 for each configuration (R1–R8). The paper also states that noise enhancement improves generalization for α not too large and reduces the small-batch/large-batch gap (R23–R28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Best accuracy comparison: fixed minibatch size 5000 with noise enhancement versus varying minibatch size without it
reader_labels.reason: The large-batch noise-enhanced setting has higher reported best accuracy for all three configurations, but the study trains to loss thresholds rather than using a fixed epoch budget (R17–R22).
